stories.title: Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion, valuation climbs to $6.2 billion
stories.summary: Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on AI inference, announced a $1.5 billion financing round that values the company at $6.2 billion, more than double its late‑2024 valuation of $2.6 billion. The round was led by Trace Capital and Innovation X, with participation from Cadence Ventures, Eclipse, Fidelity, SanDisk and T. Rowe Price. CEO Jim Keller said the funds will be used to scale chips for open‑weight AI models and video‑generation workloads.
stories.why: The capital infusion is intended to speed development of alternative AI hardware that could chip away at Nvidia’s market dominance.

stories.title: RBI tightens scrutiny of overseas investments over $1 billion
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced stricter review of overseas direct investments exceeding $1 billion by Indian companies. Banks must now collect and submit detailed information on such investments to the RBI, using a checklist that requires thorough due‑diligence of the investment rationale. The measure is intended to reduce the risk of losses to the companies and the Indian economy.

stories.title: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured after being hit by a car in Wangaratta
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a car outside her constituency office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday afternoon and is now in critical condition at a Melbourne hospital. Police detained a 43‑year‑old man from nearby Tarrawingee after a passerby intervened, and a knife was found in the vehicle. Authorities are investigating whether the act was intentional but say there is no ongoing community threat.
stories.why: The incident highlights concerns about the safety of elected officials and the potential for political violence in Australia.

stories.title: RBI injects Rs 1 lakh crore as liquidity tightens before festive season
stories.summary: On Monday, the RBI announced a Rs 1-lakh-crore variable rate repo (VRR) auction for the first time since late July after the weighted average call rate (WACR) at 5.67% on Monday, or 17 basis points higher than the repo rate of 5.50%. RBI's VRR operation attracted bids of Rs 1.50 lakh crore while the banking system liquidity stood at a surplus of Rs 1.99 lakh crore as of October 16.

stories.title: Nasdaq leads Wall Street gains as chip and AI stocks rebound
stories.summary: U.S. equities closed mixed on Monday, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 1.11% to 26,430.89 points, the S&P 500 rising 0.42% to 7,691.07 points, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipping 0.06% to 51,970.20 points. Chip and AI‑related shares rebounded, ending an eight‑session decline for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, while CoreWeave rose after a Goldman Sachs upgrade to Buy and Intel advanced after a J.P. Morgan upgrade to Neutral.
stories.why: The rebound may influence investor sentiment ahead of upcoming earnings reports.

stories.title: US President Trump lifts select Russian sanctions, easing India’s energy concerns
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a waiver of certain Russian sanctions, a move that could improve trade relations with India. India, a major importer of Russian oil, has been facing reduced imports and higher costs. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in India to discuss energy cooperation, and the waiver may give India leverage to negotiate more favorable oil tariffs.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Jio IPO draws Rs 2.5 lakh crore in anchor bids from over 70 investors
stories.summary: Jio Platforms’ Rs 30,188 cr IPO has attracted institutional bids worth around Rs 2.5 lakh cr, more than 30 times the size of its anchor book. Over 70 investors, including global asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, domestic mutual funds and insurers, have expressed interest ahead of the October 21 opening.

stories.title: Trump suspends pending Russian sanctions to keep peace talks alive
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that he blocked several Russian sanctions that were scheduled to take effect on Friday, saying the move was intended to keep Moscow at the negotiating table and facilitate peace talks over the Russia‑Ukraine war. The decision came as tensions rose with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who warned that aligning with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a “historic mistake.” Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the suspension an “important and truly historic moment,” saying the sanctions would have caused serious damage to U.S. and global markets.
stories.why: The suspension changes U.S. pressure on Russia and could influence the trajectory of the Ukraine conflict and international sanctions policy.
